decisions.choice: another disciple: a follower of Jesus whom John does not name
alternatives: a disciple who was not one of the Twelve
decisions.reason: John does not say who this disciple was. Some have identified him with the disciple whom Jesus loved, because in 20:2-8 that disciple is called "the other disciple", and there too he is paired with Peter, as he is in 13:23-24 and 21:7, 20-21. But here he is "another disciple", not "the other", and nothing in this passage calls him the disciple whom Jesus loved. His acquaintance with the high priest (verse 15b) has led others to think of a disciple from Jerusalem rather than a fisherman from Galilee. The text leaves him unnamed; a footnote mentions the identification with the disciple whom Jesus loved as possible but unproved.

decisions.choice: another disciple, without the article (SBLGNT)
alternatives: the other disciple, with the article (many later manuscripts)
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "the other disciple", which would point to a disciple the reader already knows, perhaps the one in 20:2. The older manuscripts, among them Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Vaticanus, have no article, and the article looks like an addition that made the identification easier. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: was following: the imperfect pictures them going after Jesus as he was led away
alternatives: followed as his disciples (in the sense of discipleship)
decisions.reason: The verb is the ordinary word for following someone along a road, and the imperfect shows an action going on: they were walking behind the arresting party as it took Jesus to Annas (18:12-13). The word is also John's word for following Jesus as a disciple (1:37-43; 8:12), and Peter had said he would follow Jesus even now (13:36-37); here he does follow, at a distance from the one he follows.

decisions.choice: and [so was] another disciple (L); and so was another disciple (B)
alternatives: Simon Peter and another disciple were following Jesus
decisions.reason: The Greek names Peter first and adds the other disciple at the end, almost as an afterthought; Literal and Balanced keep that order so that Peter stays at the center of the scene. Readable joins the two names as one subject.

decisions.choice: y otro discípulo, at the end (L); y también otro discípulo (B)
decisions.reason: As in English: Literal and Balanced keep the Greek order, which names Peter first and adds the other disciple at the end, so that Peter stays at the center of the scene. "Otro", not "el otro", follows the SBLGNT, which has no article (meaning decisions m1 and m2).

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B), with Literal keeping John's present tense ("dit", verses 17 and 26) and the imperfect for what was going on ("suivait", "se chauffait"); passé composé (R); speech in the passé composé at every level
alternatives: passé composé for narration at every level
decisions.reason: The French brief for the passage (18:15-27), as in 1:19. Balanced narrates in the passé simple ("entra", "nia"), the tense of written narrative; Readable uses the passé composé ("est entré", "a nié"). The many imperfects of the Greek (standing, warming himself) stay imperfect at every level.

decisions.choice: L keeps the historic present where the Greek has it ("anamwambia" 18:17, "anasema" 18:26); B tells the story with -li- for the first verb and -ka- for those that follow; R uses the plain past
decisions.reason: John tells parts of this scene in the present tense to make it vivid (English rendering decision r-en-1 at 18:17). Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable use the narrative past, which is how written Swahili tells a story. This holds for the whole passage. As elsewhere, deity_pronoun spans go only on free pronouns and possessives ("wake", "yake", "naye", "mimi"), since a verb prefix cannot take a capital.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in the Amharic
alternatives: Marking pronouns for God and Jesus in some other way
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the setting that capitalises pronouns for God and Jesus in English has nothing to change in Amharic; most such pronouns are verb suffixes in any case.

decisions.choice: known to the high priest: acquainted with him, perhaps closely
alternatives: known only by sight to the household
decisions.reason: The word means someone known to another, an acquaintance; it can be used of relatives and friends (Luke 2:44; 23:49). It was enough for the disciple to be let in himself and to have Peter let in at his word (verse 16). John does not say how the acquaintance came about.

decisions.choice: the courtyard: the open court inside the high priest's house, entered by a door from the street
decisions.reason: A large house was built around an open courtyard, closed to the street by a wall with a door kept by a doorkeeper (Acts 12:13-14). Those who were let in stood in the courtyard, and from there one could see into the rooms around it. John does not say whether Annas and Caiaphas lived in the same house; Jesus was brought to Annas first (18:13) and later sent to Caiaphas (18:24).

decisions.choice: but Peter was standing outside: a contrast with the disciple who went in
decisions.reason: The sentence sets the two disciples side by side: one goes in with Jesus, the other is left standing outside the door. The tense of "was standing" pictures Peter waiting there until the other disciple came for him.

decisions.choice: The high priest knew that disciple, so he went ...
alternatives: That disciple was known to the high priest, and he went ...
decisions.reason: Readable turns the sentence round so that it has an active verb, and says "so" because being known to the high priest is what let him in, as verse 16 shows.

decisions.choice: el patio (every level); de la casa (R); El sumo sacerdote conocía a ese discípulo, así que (R)
decisions.reason: "Patio" is the open court inside a house (meaning decision m2); "atrio" is kept for the temple courts. As in English, Readable turns the sentence round with an active verb and says "así que", since being known is what let him in.

decisions.choice: ua wa kuhani mkuu (L); ua wa nyumba ya kuhani mkuu (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Ua" is the enclosed open court of a house (meaning decision m2). Balanced and Readable add "wa nyumba" so that it is plainly the court inside the high priest's house, not an open yard.

decisions.choice: "中庭" for the courtyard; "戸口" (L), "門" (B, R) for its door
decisions.reason: The courtyard is the open court inside the house, closed to the street by a wall and a kept door (m2). 中庭 names it; at Balanced and Readable the street door of such a court is a 門 in Japanese, while Literal keeps the plain word for a door.

source.text: ἐξῆλθεν οὖν ὁ μαθητὴς ὁ ἄλλος ὁ γνωστὸς τοῦ ἀρχιερέως καὶ εἶπεν τῇ θυρωρῷ καὶ εἰσήγαγεν τὸν Πέτρον.

records.literal_gloss: Went out therefore the disciple the other the [one] known of the high priest and spoke to the doorkeeper and brought in Peter.

en.L: So the other disciple, the one known to the high priest, went out and spoke to the doorkeeper and brought Peter in.
en.B: So the other disciple, the one known to the high priest, went out, spoke to the woman who kept the door, and brought Peter in.
en.R: So the other disciple, the one the high priest knew, came back out. He spoke to the young woman who was watching the door, and then he brought Peter inside.

es.L: Salió, pues, el otro discípulo, el conocido del sumo sacerdote, y habló a la portera, e hizo entrar a Pedro.
es.B: Entonces el otro discípulo, el que era conocido del sumo sacerdote, salió, habló con la portera e hizo entrar a Pedro.
es.R: Entonces el otro discípulo, el que el sumo sacerdote conocía, volvió a salir. Habló con la muchacha que cuidaba la puerta, y luego hizo entrar a Pedro.

fr.L: L’autre disciple, celui qui était connu du grand prêtre, sortit donc, et parla à la portière, et fit entrer Pierre.
fr.B: L’autre disciple, celui qui était connu du grand prêtre, ressortit donc, parla à la femme qui gardait la porte et fit entrer Pierre.
fr.R: Alors l’autre disciple, celui que le grand prêtre connaissait, est ressorti. Il a parlé à la jeune femme qui surveillait la porte, puis il a fait entrer Pierre.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo mwanafunzi yule mwingine, yule anayefahamika kwa kuhani mkuu, alitoka nje na kuzungumza na mlinzi wa mlango, kisha akamwingiza Petro.

sw.R: Basi yule mwanafunzi mwingine, ambaye kuhani mkuu alimfahamu, alitoka nje tena. Akazungumza na msichana aliyekuwa akilinda mlango, kisha akamwingiza Petro ndani.

decisions.choice: brought Peter in: the other disciple is the one who brings him in
decisions.reason: The verb does not show who its subject is, and the doorkeeper has just been mentioned. But the other disciple is the subject of the two verbs before it (went out, spoke), and the sentence reads most naturally with him as the subject of all three. Either way, Peter is let in because of the other disciple.

decisions.choice: the doorkeeper: a woman whose task was to keep the door of the house
decisions.reason: The article with the word is feminine, and verse 17 says that the doorkeeper was a slave girl. Women kept the door of a house in other stories too (Acts 12:13; 2 Samuel 4:6 in the Greek version).

decisions.choice: the woman who kept the door (B); the young woman who was watching the door (R)
decisions.reason: "Doorkeeper" does not show that this was a woman, which the Greek article does (meaning decision m2). Balanced and Readable say so here, so that the servant girl in verse 17 is clearly the same person.

decisions.choice: la portera (L, B); la muchacha que cuidaba la puerta (R)
decisions.reason: Spanish "portera" is feminine, so Literal and Balanced show that the doorkeeper was a woman (meaning decision m2) without the longer phrase English needs; Readable says it in plain words, so that she is clearly the girl of verse 17.

decisions.choice: a porteira
decisions.reason: Portuguese has a feminine noun for a woman who keeps a door, so Literal can show what the Greek article shows (meaning decision m2) without the explanation the English Literal lacks; Balanced and Readable say "a moça que cuidava da porta", as the English does.

decisions.choice: "द्वारपालिन" (L); "द्वार की रखवाली करनेवाली स्त्री" (B); "द्वार पर पहरा देनेवाली लड़की" (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is feminine (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps the one word in its feminine form; Balanced and Readable say what she did, since "द्वारपालिन" is uncommon in everyday Hindi.

decisions.choice: "привратница" (L, B)
decisions.reason: Russian has a feminine form for the doorkeeper, so the woman of verse 17 is plain at once (meaning decision m2) without the English Balanced's longer phrase.

decisions.choice: slave girl: a young female slave of the household
decisions.reason: The word is the feminine of the word for a young slave and was the usual word for a female slave, often a young one (Acts 12:13; 16:16; Galatians 4:22-23). She belonged to the high priest's household, as did the male slaves in verses 18 and 26. She is one of the lowest people in the house, and it is her question that Peter cannot answer truthfully.

decisions.choice: a question that expects the answer no
decisions.reason: The word that opens the question shows that the speaker expects a denial: "You are not ..., are you?" The question leaves Peter an easy way out, and he takes it. The same form returns in verse 25.

decisions.choice: also: you too, as well as the other disciple, or as well as others who follow him
decisions.reason: "Also" may mean that the doorkeeper knew the other disciple to be a follower of Jesus, since he had just spoken with her and brought Peter in; or it may simply mean "you as well as the man's other followers". The text does not settle it.

decisions.choice: this man: Jesus, named without his name
decisions.reason: The doorkeeper speaks of Jesus as "this man", the prisoner who has just been brought in. The phrase can carry contempt (9:16, 24), but here it need be no more than a way of pointing to the man under arrest.

decisions.choice: says (L); said (B, R); also verse 26
decisions.reason: John often tells past events in the present tense ("says") to make a scene vivid. Literal keeps the present; Balanced and Readable use the past, as stories are normally told. This applies to every such verb in the passage ("says" twice in verse 17 and once in verse 26).

decisions.choice: servant girl
decisions.reason: "Servant girl" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it for a female slave; the meaning decision (m1) keeps that she was owned, and Literal keeps "slave girl".

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal (dice); pretérito at Balanced and Readable; la esclava (L), la criada (B, R)
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in John: Literal keeps John's present, Balanced and Readable use the pretérito; this applies throughout the passage. Literal keeps "esclava" (meaning decision m1). The feminine of "siervo" is rare in modern Spanish, so Balanced and Readable say "criada", the ordinary word for a girl serving in a household.

decisions.choice: ¿Acaso también tú eres ...? (L); Tú no eres también ..., ¿verdad? (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek question expects the answer no (meaning decision m2). Spanish "¿No eres tú también ...?" would expect yes, so Literal uses "¿Acaso ...?" and Balanced and Readable a statement with "¿verdad?". The same form returns in verse 25.

decisions.choice: la jeune esclave (L); la servante (B, R); likewise les esclaves (L), les serviteurs (B, R) in verses 18 and 26
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for this word: Literal keeps "esclave", and Balanced and Readable say "servante", "serviteurs", as the English does, since her place in the household, not slavery itself, is the point (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: Tu n’es pas, toi aussi, ... ? (a statement with a question mark)
decisions.reason: The Greek question expects the answer no (meaning decision m2). In French "N’es-tu pas ... ?" expects yes, so every level asks with the word order of a statement, which leaves the expected answer open or negative, as the English tag "are you?" does. The same in verse 25.

decisions.choice: a negative statement with the tag "sivyo?" ("Wewe pia hu ..., sivyo?"); also verse 25
decisions.reason: The Greek question expects the answer no (meaning decision m2), like the English "You are not ..., are you?". A question opened with "Je ... si" would expect yes in Swahili, and a plain "Je, ... ni" would not show any expectation. A reviewer should confirm that the tag reads as expecting a denial.

decisions.choice: kijakazi (L); mtumishi wa kike (B); msichana mtumishi (R)
decisions.reason: "Kijakazi" is a young female slave, the sense of the Greek (meaning decision m1). Balanced and Readable say "servant", as for the male slaves (mtumishi), and Readable says she was a girl.

decisions.choice: "anh" for Peter and "tôi" for himself in the courtyard; "người này", "ông ta" for Jesus
decisions.reason: Ordinary people among themselves use the plain "anh" and "tôi", as the style guide says; those who do not follow Jesus speak of him as "người này" or "ông ta", with no honorific and no setting (verses 17, 25, 26). Literal keeps the historic present "nói" (says) by leaving out "đã", here and in verse 26.

decisions.choice: cô gái nô lệ (L); cô đầy tớ gái (B, R)
decisions.reason: The style guide's "nô lệ" (L) and "đầy tớ" (B, R) for slaves, with the word for a young woman; "nữ tỳ" is archaic.

decisions.choice: Historic present kept at Literal (말한다); past at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: John tells this in the present (also verse 26); Literal keeps it, Balanced and Readable use the narrative past (one decision for the passage).

decisions.choice: 설마 ... 아니겠지? in the plain style (해라체) for the questions put to Peter (also verses 25 and 26)
decisions.reason: 설마 ... 아니겠지 asks a question that expects "no", as the Greek does; the household and guards speak to Peter as equals or with suspicion, and Peter answers in the same style.

decisions.choice: 여종 for paidiskē at every level
decisions.reason: 여종 matches 종 for doulos; 계집종 is old and demeaning, and 하녀 suggests modern domestic service.

decisions.choice: a criada (L, B); a empregada (R)
decisions.reason: "Criada" is the Portuguese word for a girl serving in a household, as in Matthew 26:69, and it is the word that tells this story in Portuguese. Literal does not say "escrava" here because "criada" already implies she belonged to the household (meaning decision m1). Readable says "empregada", the everyday word.

decisions.choice: Por acaso também você ...? (L); Você não é também ..., é? (B, R)
decisions.reason: The question expects "no" (meaning decision m2). Literal marks this with "Por acaso"; Balanced and Readable use the Brazilian tag question "..., é?", which asks for a denial in the same way.

decisions.choice: "ገረድ" (servant girl) at every level
decisions.reason: "ገረድ" is a young woman in household service, the word Matthew 26:69 uses for the same Greek word; "ሴት ባሪያ" is heavy for a doorkeeper named in passing.

decisions.choice: "... አይደለህም፣ አይደል?" (you are not ..., are you?) for a question that expects "no"; also 18:25
decisions.reason: Amharic marks the expected answer with the tag "አይደል?" after a negative statement, as the Greek marks it with its particle; a plain question would lose the hint.

decisions.choice: "कहती है" (L); "कहा" (B, R), and likewise through the passage
decisions.reason: John tells past events in the present tense here ("says"). Literal keeps the historic present, Balanced and Readable use the past (docs/john-terms.md); one decision for the passage.
The question expects the answer no (meaning decision m2). Hindi shows that with "तो नहीं", so the girl's question is a tentative suggestion, not a plain inquiry.

decisions.choice: "говорит" (L); "сказала" (B, R)
decisions.reason: John tells past events in the present (historic present), here and in verses 17b and 26. Literal keeps it; Balanced and Readable use the past. One note for the passage.

decisions.choice: "служанка"
decisions.reason: Russian "служанка" is the usual word for a girl in a household's service, as in Matthew 26:69; Literal keeps the "-ка" of the Greek diminutive.

decisions.choice: "служниця" at every level ("служниця-воротарка" at L)
decisions.reason: The passion term settled in Mark: "служниця" is the natural word for a young woman serving in a household; Literal adds her task at the door, as the Greek does.

decisions.choice: "奴隷の娘" (L); "召し使いの女" (B, R); "まさか……ではないでしょうね" for the question expecting no
decisions.reason: The word is a young female slave (m1); Literal says so and Balanced and Readable say servant, as with doulos. The opening particle expects a denial (m2): まさか with でしょうね asks in a way that invites "no", and the mild politeness fits a household servant speaking to a stranger. Historic presents in 18:15-27 ("言う") stay present at Literal only.

records.literal_gloss: Says that one, Not I am.

fr.L: Celui-ci dit : « Je ne [le] suis pas. »
fr.B: Il dit : « Je ne le suis pas. »
fr.R: « Non, je ne le suis pas », a dit Pierre.

hi.R: "नहीं, मैं नहीं हूँ," पतरस ने कहा।

ru.R: «Нет, я не из них», — сказал Пётр.

ja.L: 彼は言う。「わたしは[そう]ではない。」
ja.B: 彼は「わたしはそうではない」と言った。
ja.R: 「いや、わたしは違う」とペトロは言いました。

decisions.choice: I am not: Peter's words stand in contrast with Jesus's "I am" in the garden
alternatives: an ordinary denial with no further meaning
decisions.reason: A few verses earlier Jesus answered those who came to arrest him with "I am" (18:5, 6, 8), giving himself up so that his disciples could go free (18:8-9). Now Peter, asked whether he belongs to Jesus, says the same two words with a "not": "I am not." John tells the two scenes one after the other, and the contrast is plain on the page. Whether John meant it as a deliberate echo cannot be proved, since "I am not" is also the ordinary way to say "no" to such a question. John the Baptist used the same words truthfully when he denied that he was the Christ (1:20-21).

decisions.choice: that one: Peter
decisions.reason: The pronoun points back to Peter, to whom the question was put. It is the first of the three denials Jesus foretold (13:38).

decisions.choice: "No, I am not," Peter said.
decisions.reason: Readable names Peter and adds "No" to make the answer sound natural, and keeps "I am not" so that the words match those in verse 25.

decisions.choice: No soy (L); No lo soy (B); No, no lo soy ... Pedro (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the bare "No soy", which sets Peter's words against Jesus's "Yo soy" in verses 5-8 (meaning decision m1). Balanced and Readable add "lo", as natural Spanish does (1:21); Readable names Peter.

decisions.choice: Je ne [le] suis pas (L); Je ne le suis pas (B, R); also verse 25
decisions.reason: French repeats the predicate with "le" in a short answer, as in 1:21, and Literal brackets it. The words mirror Jesus's "Je [le] suis" in the garden (18:5, 8), the contrast meaning decision m1 points to.

decisions.choice: Mimi siye; also verse 25
decisions.reason: "Mimi siye" (I am not the one) is the negative of "Mimi ndiye", Jesus's words in 18:5-8, so the contrast John sets up (meaning decision m1) is as plain in Swahili as in the Greek. Swahili needs the free pronoun "mimi" with this copula, so it is not bracketed at Literal.

decisions.choice: Tôi không phải
decisions.reason: "Tôi không phải" is the plain denial that stands against Jesus's "Ta là [người đó]" in verses 5-8; "Không phải tôi" would mean "it was not me".

decisions.choice: Não sou (also verse 25)
decisions.reason: Portuguese answers with the verb alone, "Não sou", which stands against Jesus's "Eu sou" in verses 5-8 word for word (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: "አይደለሁም" (I am not) at every level; also 18:25
decisions.reason: "አይደለሁም" is the negative of "እኔ ነኝ", so Peter's "I am not" stands against Jesus's "I am" in 18:5-8 in Amharic as in Greek.
Peter's words stand against Jesus's "I am" in the garden (meaning decision m1). Every level keeps the full "मैं नहीं हूँ", so that it answers "मैं वही हूँ" in 18:5-8.

decisions.choice: "Нет, не я" (L, B)
decisions.reason: Peter's "I am not" is set against Jesus's "I am" in the garden (meaning decision m1); "не я" answers "Это я" of 18:5-8 as closely as Russian allows. Readable says the plain answer and keeps it the same in verse 25.

decisions.choice: "わたしは[そう]ではない" (L); "わたしはそうではない" (B); "わたしは違う" (R); also 18:25
decisions.reason: Peter's words stand against Jesus's "I am" in the garden (m1). Keeping "わたしは……ではない" lets the reader hear it against "わたしである" in 18:5-8. "わたしではない" would mean "it was not me".

source.text: εἱστήκεισαν δὲ οἱ δοῦλοι καὶ οἱ ὑπηρέται ἀνθρακιὰν πεποιηκότες, ὅτι ψῦχος ἦν, καὶ ἐθερμαίνοντο· ἦν δὲ καὶ ὁ Πέτρος μετ’ αὐτῶν ἑστὼς καὶ θερμαινόμενος.

records.literal_gloss: Were standing now the slaves and the officers, a charcoal fire having made, because cold it was, and they were warming themselves; was now also Peter with them standing and warming himself.

en.L: Now the slaves and the officers were standing [there], having made a charcoal fire, because it was cold, and they were warming themselves; and Peter also was with them, standing and warming himself.
en.B: The servants and the temple police had made a charcoal fire, because it was cold, and they were standing around it warming themselves. Peter was standing with them too, warming himself.
en.R: It was cold, so the servants and the temple guards had made a charcoal fire. They stood around it to keep warm. Peter stood there with them, warming himself too.

es.L: Y estaban de pie los esclavos y los alguaciles, que habían hecho un fuego de brasas, porque hacía frío, y se calentaban; y estaba también Pedro con ellos, de pie y calentándose.
es.B: Los siervos y los guardias del templo habían hecho un fuego de brasas, porque hacía frío, y estaban de pie a su alrededor calentándose. Pedro también estaba con ellos, de pie, calentándose.
es.R: Hacía frío, así que los siervos y los guardias del templo habían encendido un fuego de brasas. Estaban alrededor del fuego para calentarse. Pedro también estaba allí con ellos, calentándose.

fr.L: Or les esclaves et les gardes se tenaient [là], ayant fait un feu de braises, parce qu’il faisait froid, et ils se chauffaient ; et Pierre aussi était avec eux, debout, et se chauffait.
fr.B: Les serviteurs et les gardes du temple avaient fait un feu de braises, parce qu’il faisait froid, et ils se tenaient autour pour se chauffer. Pierre se tenait avec eux, lui aussi, et se chauffait.
fr.R: Il faisait froid, alors les serviteurs et les gardes du temple avaient allumé un feu de braises. Ils se tenaient autour pour se réchauffer. Pierre était là avec eux, et il se réchauffait aussi.

sw.L: Basi watumwa na walinzi walikuwa wamesimama [pale], baada ya kuwasha moto wa makaa kwa sababu kulikuwa na baridi, wakijipasha joto; Petro naye alikuwa pamoja nao, amesimama na kujipasha joto.
sw.B: Watumishi na walinzi wa hekalu walikuwa wamewasha moto wa makaa kwa sababu kulikuwa na baridi, wakasimama kuuzunguka wakijipasha joto. Petro pia alikuwa amesimama pamoja nao, akijipasha joto.
sw.R: Kulikuwa na baridi, kwa hiyo watumishi na walinzi wa hekalu walikuwa wamewasha moto wa makaa. Walisimama kuuzunguka ili kupata joto. Petro naye alisimama pale pamoja nao, akijipasha joto pia.

vi.L: Vả, các nô lệ và các cảnh vệ đã nhóm một đống lửa than và đứng [đó], vì trời lạnh, và họ sưởi ấm; Phi-e-rơ cũng đứng với họ và sưởi ấm.
vi.B: Các đầy tớ và lính canh đền thờ đã đốt một đống lửa than, vì trời lạnh, và họ đứng quanh đó sưởi ấm. Phi-e-rơ cũng đứng với họ mà sưởi.
vi.R: Trời lạnh, nên các đầy tớ và lính canh đền thờ đốt một đống lửa than. Họ đứng quanh đống lửa cho ấm. Phi-e-rơ cũng đứng đó với họ và sưởi ấm.

ko.L: 그런데 종들과 경비병들이 숯불을 피워 놓고 [거기] 서 있었다. 날이 추웠기 때문이다. 그들은 불을 쬐고 있었고, 베드로도 그들과 함께 서서 불을 쬐고 있었다.
ko.B: 날이 추워서 종들과 성전 경비병들이 숯불을 피워 놓고 둘러서서 불을 쬐고 있었다. 베드로도 그들과 함께 서서 불을 쬐고 있었다.
ko.R: 날씨가 추웠다. 그래서 종들과 성전 경비병들이 숯불을 피워 놓고 그 둘레에 서서 몸을 녹이고 있었다. 베드로도 그들과 함께 서서 몸을 녹였다.

pt.L: E os escravos e os guardas estavam de pé, tendo feito um fogo de brasas, porque fazia frio, e se aqueciam; e também Pedro estava com eles, de pé e se aquecendo.
pt.B: Os servos e os guardas do templo tinham feito um fogo de brasas, porque fazia frio, e estavam de pé em volta dele, se aquecendo. Pedro também estava de pé com eles, se aquecendo.
pt.R: Fazia frio, e por isso os servos e os guardas do templo tinham feito um fogo de brasas. Eles ficaram em volta do fogo para se esquentar. Pedro também ficou ali com eles, se esquentando.

hi.L: और दास और पहरेदार, कोयलों की आग जलाकर, [वहाँ] खड़े थे, क्योंकि ठंड थी, और वे ताप रहे थे; और पतरस भी उनके साथ खड़ा होकर ताप रहा था।

ru.L: Стояли же рабы и служители, разведя костёр из углей, потому что было холодно, и грелись; был же и Пётр с ними, стоя и греясь.
ru.B: Рабы и храмовая стража развели костёр из углей, потому что было холодно, и стояли вокруг него, грелись. Пётр тоже стоял с ними и грелся.
ru.R: Было холодно, и рабы с храмовыми стражниками развели костёр из углей. Они стояли вокруг него, чтобы согреться. Пётр стоял там вместе с ними и тоже грелся.

uk.B: Раби й храмові вартові розклали вогнище з вугілля, бо було холодно, і стояли довкола, гріючись. Петро теж стояв з ними й грівся.
uk.R: Було холодно, тож слуги й храмові вартові розклали вогнище з вугілля. Вони стояли довкола нього, щоб зігрітися. Петро стояв там разом з ними і теж грівся.

ja.L: さて、奴隷たちと下役たちは、炭火を起こして立っていた。寒かったからである。そして彼らは暖まっていた。ペトロも彼らとともにいて、立って暖まっていた。
ja.B: 寒かったので、しもべたちや神殿の警備兵たちは炭火を起こし、その周りに立って暖まっていた。ペトロも彼らといっしょに立って、暖まっていた。
ja.R: 寒かったので、しもべたちと神殿の警備兵たちは炭火をたいていました。そして、そのまわりに立って暖まっていました。ペトロも彼らといっしょに立って、暖まっていました。

id.L: Budak-budak dan penjaga-penjaga berdiri di situ setelah membuat api arang, karena hari dingin, dan mereka berdiang; dan Petrus juga berdiri bersama mereka dan berdiang.
id.B: Hamba-hamba dan penjaga-penjaga Bait Allah telah membuat api arang, karena udara dingin, lalu mereka berdiri di sekelilingnya untuk menghangatkan badan. Petrus juga berdiri bersama mereka dan menghangatkan badan.
id.R: Udara dingin, jadi hamba-hamba dan penjaga-penjaga Bait Allah membuat api arang. Mereka berdiri di sekelilingnya untuk menghangatkan badan. Petrus juga berdiri di sana bersama mereka dan menghangatkan badan.

decisions.choice: slaves: the high priest's household slaves
decisions.reason: These are slaves of the high priest's household, like Malchus (18:10) and his relative (verse 26), and the slave girl at the door (verse 17). A wealthy household such as the high priest's had many slaves, who served in the house and on its business; their master owned them, and they had no freedom of their own.

decisions.choice: the officers: the temple police who had made the arrest
decisions.reason: These are the officers of the chief priests who came with Judas and arrested Jesus (18:3, 12), the men who kept order in the temple for the priests (7:32, 45-46). The Roman soldiers who had also been there (18:3, 12) are not mentioned here.

decisions.choice: a charcoal fire, because it was cold: a fire of glowing coals on a cold spring night
decisions.reason: The word means a heap of burning charcoal, which gives heat and a little light. Passover falls in early spring, and Jerusalem stands high in the hills, so the nights can be cold. The fire draws Peter into the circle of the men who had arrested Jesus.

decisions.choice: a charcoal fire: the same word as in 21:9, where the risen Jesus restores Peter
alternatives: no connection between the two scenes
decisions.reason: This word is used only twice in the New Testament: here, where Peter denies Jesus three times, and in 21:9, where the risen Jesus has a charcoal fire burning by the lake before he asks Peter three times whether he loves him (21:15-17). John may mean the reader to remember this fire there. The link rests on one word, so it cannot be proved.

decisions.choice: temple police (B); temple guards (R)
decisions.reason: As in 7:32 and 7:45, Balanced and Readable say whose officers these were (meaning decision m2). The household slaves are "servants" in Balanced and Readable (style guide), kept apart from the temple police or guards.

decisions.choice: had made a charcoal fire ... standing around it (B); It was cold, so ... (R)
alternatives: were standing, having made a charcoal fire (Literal)
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the making of the fire first, since it came first, and says they stood "around it", which the Greek implies. Readable gives the reason first, in its own sentence.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m1) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

decisions.choice: los esclavos, los alguaciles (L); los siervos, los guardias del templo (B, R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide renderings, as at 7:32 and 13:16: the household slaves (meaning decision m1) are kept apart from the temple police (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: un fuego de brasas
decisions.reason: A fire of glowing charcoal (meaning decision m3). Every level uses the same words so that the fire of 21:9 can be recognized (meaning decision m4); "hoguera" suggests flames and "brasero" a pan of coals.

decisions.choice: un feu de braises
decisions.reason: The word is a fire of glowing coals, and it occurs again only in 21:9, where the risen Jesus restores Peter (meaning decision m4); every level uses the same plain words so that 21:9 can repeat them. "Feu de charbon" would suggest mineral coal.

decisions.choice: moto wa makaa (every level); watumwa (L), watumishi (B, R); walinzi (L), walinzi wa hekalu (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Moto wa makaa" is a fire of glowing charcoal (meaning decision m3), and the same words are used at 21:9, so the echo noted in meaning decision m4 is kept. The slaves and the temple police are named as in 18:3 and 18:10.

decisions.choice: 숯불 for "a charcoal fire" at every level
decisions.reason: The Greek word returns only in 21:9, where the risen Jesus restores Peter; using 숯불 in both places lets the Korean reader hear the link the meaning note describes.

decisions.choice: um fogo de brasas
decisions.reason: "Fogo de brasas" says what the Greek word means, a fire of glowing coals (meaning decision m3), and is a plain phrase that can be used again where the same word returns in 21:9 (m4). "Fogueira" suggests a blazing wood fire.

decisions.choice: "ባሪያዎች" (slaves) at every level; "ዘበኞች" (L), "የቤተ መቅደስ ዘበኞች" (B), "የቤተ መቅደስ ጠባቂዎች" (R); also 18:26
decisions.reason: As in 18:10, the style guide keeps "ባሪያ" for the Greek word at every level; the officers have the words given at 18:3.

decisions.choice: "कोयलों की आग"
decisions.reason: A fire of glowing coals; every level keeps "कोयलों की आग" so the same words can return in 21:9, where the Greek word recurs (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: "костёр из углей"
decisions.reason: The Greek names a fire of charcoal, the word used again in 21:9 where the risen Jesus restores Peter (meaning decision m4); every level keeps "из углей" so the echo stays.

decisions.choice: "рабы" (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Раб" for doulos at every level (style guide), where the English Balanced and Readable say "servants".

decisions.choice: "вогнище з вугілля" at every level, also in John 21:9
decisions.reason: The Greek word, a charcoal fire, appears only here and at 21:9, where the risen Jesus restores Peter by another charcoal fire; the same Ukrainian words at both places keep the echo.

decisions.choice: "炭火" at every level
decisions.reason: The word is a fire of charcoal (m3), and the same rare word returns in 21:9 (m4); 炭火 keeps it the same at every level so the link can be seen.

decisions.choice: the high priest: Annas, who is questioning Jesus before he sends him to Caiaphas
alternatives: Caiaphas, the high priest of that year (18:13)
decisions.reason: Jesus was taken "first" to Annas (18:13), and only after this questioning did Annas send him to Caiaphas (verse 24), so the questioner here is most naturally Annas. Annas had been high priest some years before (about AD 6 to 15) and was the father-in-law of Caiaphas (18:13). Former high priests kept the title, and Annas remained powerful: five of his sons became high priest. Luke too calls him high priest alongside Caiaphas (Luke 3:2; Acts 4:6). Others read "the high priest" here as Caiaphas, who is called that in 18:13 and 24; a footnote gives that view.

decisions.choice: So: John returns from the courtyard to Jesus
decisions.reason: The word picks up the story of Jesus where it left off in 18:13-14, while Peter is in the courtyard. John moves between the two scenes, Peter's denials (verses 15-18 and 25-27) and Jesus's questioning (verses 19-24), so that the reader sees both at once: Jesus stands firm while Peter gives way.

decisions.choice: about his disciples and his teaching: who his followers were and what he taught them
decisions.reason: The questions seem meant to find grounds for a charge: how large his following was, and whether his teaching led people astray (7:12, 47). Jesus answers about his teaching and says nothing about his disciples, the ones he had protected at his arrest (18:8-9).

decisions.choice: openly: in public, where anyone could hear
decisions.reason: The word means openness in speech, and here, set against "in secret" at the end of the verse, it means in public. It is the word used when Jesus taught openly in the temple (7:26) and when he stopped going about openly (11:54). In 10:24 and 16:25, 29 it means plain speech instead; that is not the sense here.

decisions.choice: the world: people at large, anyone who would listen
alternatives: the world as opposed to God (15:18)
decisions.reason: Here the world is simply everyone: Jesus did not teach a closed circle but spoke where all could hear (compare 7:4, where his brothers told him to show himself to the world).

decisions.choice: the Jews: the Jewish people, who gathered in the synagogues and the temple
decisions.reason: Here the word means the Jewish people as a whole, who came together for worship and teaching in their synagogues and, at the festivals, in the temple in Jerusalem. Jesus taught them all in the open (6:59; 7:14, 28; 10:23). It does not mean the authorities, so every level keeps "the Jews".

decisions.choice: in synagogue: in synagogues, wherever he taught
decisions.reason: The word has no article, which gives a general sense: in synagogue gatherings, such as the one at Capernaum (6:59). The temple has the article, because there was only one.

decisions.choice: I said nothing in secret: possibly an echo of God's words in Isaiah
alternatives: no allusion; a plain statement of fact
decisions.reason: In Isaiah 45:19 and 48:16 God says that he has not spoken in secret. Jesus's words may echo these, but they are also a plain answer to a hearing held at night, away from the crowds: what he taught was never hidden.

decisions.choice: synagogues; temple courts
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the plural for the general sense of the word without an article (meaning decision m4), and say "temple courts" for the whole temple area, as John's word means (see docs/john-terms.md).

decisions.choice: en sinagoga (L), en las sinagogas (B, R); el templo (L), los atrios del templo (B), el patio del templo (R); los judíos (every level)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek without the article; Balanced and Readable use the plural for its general sense (meaning decision m4) and the words for the temple area used throughout John. Here the word means the Jewish people (meaning decision m3), so every level keeps "los judíos".

decisions.choice: tous les Juifs, at every level
decisions.reason: Here the word means the Jewish people who gathered in the synagogues and the temple (meaning decision m3), not the authorities, so every level keeps "les Juifs".

decisions.choice: en synagogue, dans le temple (L); dans les synagogues, dans la cour du temple (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek singular without an article, which French allows in "en synagogue", and "temple" for the whole temple area. Balanced and Readable follow the book-wide choice for this word, "la cour du temple", the open courts where Jesus taught, and say "synagogues" in the plural (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: Wayahudi at every level; hekaluni (L), nyua za hekalu (B), uwanja wa hekalu (R)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the Jewish people who gathered for worship (meaning decision m3), so every level keeps "Wayahudi", unlike verses 12 and 14 of this chapter. The temple area is named as at 7:14.

decisions.choice: cho mọi người (R)
decisions.reason: Here "the world" means people at large, as the meaning decision says, not humanity set against God; Readable says it plainly so that "thế gian" is not misread.

decisions.choice: mọi người Do Thái, at every level
alternatives: các nhà lãnh đạo Do Thái
decisions.reason: The Jewish people who gathered to hear him are meant, not the authorities, so Balanced and Readable keep "người Do Thái".

decisions.choice: Jesus answers the high priest in the plain style (해라체)
decisions.reason: The guide gives Jesus 해라체 with opponents; he answers his judge as one who has nothing to hide, as he does with Pilate (18:33-38).

decisions.choice: 성전 (L), 성전 뜰 (B, R) for hieron; 유대인 at every level
decisions.reason: Here "the Jews" are the people who gather to worship, so every level keeps 유대인 (docs/john-terms.md); hieron follows the guide's temple words.

decisions.choice: para todo mundo ouvir
decisions.reason: "O mundo" here means everyone (meaning decision m2). Readable says it with the everyday Brazilian "todo mundo" ("everybody"), so that the key term "o mundo" is not misread; Literal and Balanced keep "ao mundo".

decisions.choice: "አይሁድ" (the Jews) at every level here
decisions.reason: Here the word means the Jewish people who gathered in the synagogues and the temple, so Balanced and Readable keep "አይሁድ" too, following John's book-wide rule.

decisions.choice: "ምኩራብ" (synagogue); "ቤተ መቅደስ" (temple, L), "የቤተ መቅደሱ ግቢ" (the temple courts, B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word here is the whole temple area, where Jesus taught in public; Balanced and Readable say so, as in Matthew 26:55.

decisions.choice: Jesus says तुम to the high priest; the high priest's men say आप to Jesus (18:22)
decisions.reason: Jesus speaking to anyone says तुम (style guide, section 4), as he does to Pilate in Matthew 27:11 in Hindi; those who speak to him say आप, opponents included.

decisions.choice: "मन्दिर" (L); "मन्दिर के आँगनों" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word here is hieron, the whole temple area (docs/john-terms.md): Literal says "मन्दिर", Balanced and Readable say where he taught, the temple courts.

decisions.choice: "संसार के सामने" (R)
decisions.reason: The world here means people at large (meaning decision m2); Readable keeps the key term "संसार", as at every level through John and as the English Readable keeps "the world", and "के सामने" (before) makes it plain that he spoke in public.

decisions.choice: "иудеи" at every level
decisions.reason: Here the word means the Jewish people who gathered for worship (meaning decision m3), so Balanced and Readable keep "иудеи" too.

decisions.choice: "во дворах Храма" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word here (hieron) is the whole temple area, where Jesus taught in the open courts; Literal keeps "Храм".

decisions.choice: "храм" (L); "храмові двори" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word here is the whole temple area, where teachers gathered hearers in the courts; Balanced and Readable say so, as the John terms do.

decisions.choice: Jesus answers the high priest in the plain style ("語ってきた", "なぜわたしに尋ねるのか"), and the officer in 18:22 speaks plainly
alternatives: "話してきました" (です・ます) to the high priest
decisions.reason: An accused man would normally speak politely to a high priest, but here Jesus answers with authority and turns the hearing back on his questioner (18:21, 18:23). The plain style keeps that, as Jesus speaks plainly throughout the Gospel.

decisions.choice: "公然と" (L, B), "何も隠さずに" (R); "ユダヤ人たち" (L), "ユダヤ人" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Openly means in public (m1); Readable says it in everyday words. "The Jews" here are the Jewish people (m3), so Balanced and Readable say ユダヤ人, not the leaders.

decisions.choice: why question me: a case was to be proved by witnesses
alternatives: a refusal to answer anything at all
decisions.reason: In the law of Moses a charge had to be established by the evidence of witnesses (Deuteronomy 17:6; 19:15), and Jesus himself speaks of the need for witnesses (8:17). He asks why he is being questioned when there are witnesses to hand, and points to them in the next sentence. He does not refuse to speak; he asks for a fair hearing.

decisions.choice: asking me these questions
decisions.reason: Readable says "these questions" so that the plain verb "ask" keeps the sense of questioning.

decisions.choice: "ông" for the high priest
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to one official, an older man of rank, as "ông": respectful but not deferential, as the style guide sets for one person.

decisions.choice: você (Jesus to the high priest and to the guard, verses 21-23)
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to people with "você" (style section 4), as he answers the high priest in Matthew 26:64. "O senhor" would make him address the high priest as an inferior to a superior, which his answer does not do.

ru.L: Когда же {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} сказал это, один из стоявших рядом служителей дал Иисусу пощёчину, сказав: «Так отвечаешь первосвященнику?»
ru.B: Когда {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} сказал это, один из храмовых стражников, стоявший рядом, ударил Иисуса по лицу и сказал: «Так ты отвечаешь первосвященнику?»
ru.R: Когда Иисус сказал это, один из храмовых стражников, стоявших рядом, ударил {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} по лицу. «Разве так отвечают первосвященнику?» — сказал он.

uk.L: А коли {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} це сказав, один із прислужників, що стояв поруч, дав Ісусові ляпаса, кажучи: «Так відповідаєш первосвященикові?»
uk.B: Коли {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} сказав це, один із храмових вартових, що стояв поблизу, вдарив Ісуса по обличчю й сказав: «Так {{deity_pronoun:ти|Ти}} відповідаєш первосвященикові?»
uk.R: Коли Ісус сказав це, один із храмових вартових, що стояли там, дав {{deity_pronoun:йому|Йому}} ляпаса. «Хіба так відповідають первосвященикові?» — сказав він.

ja.L: イエスがこれらのことを言われると、そばに立っていた下役の一人が、イエスに平手打ちを加えて言った。「大祭司にそのように答えるのか？」
ja.B: イエスがこう言われると、そばに立っていた神殿の警備兵の一人がイエスを平手で打って、「大祭司にそんな答え方をするのか？」と言った。
ja.R: イエスがこう言われると、そこに立っていた神殿の警備兵の一人が、イエスを平手で打ちました。「大祭司に向かって、そんな答え方があるか？」とその男は言いました。

id.L: Ketika {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} mengatakan hal itu, salah seorang penjaga yang berdiri di situ menampar Yesus, katanya, "Begitukah {{deity_pronoun:engkau|Engkau}} menjawab imam besar?"
id.B: Ketika {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} mengatakan hal itu, salah seorang penjaga Bait Allah yang berdiri di dekat situ menampar Yesus dan berkata, "Begitukah caranya {{deity_pronoun:engkau|Engkau}} menjawab imam besar?"
id.R: Ketika Yesus berkata begitu, salah seorang penjaga Bait Allah yang berdiri di situ menampar {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}}. "Begitukah caranya menjawab imam besar?" katanya.

decisions.choice: gave a slap: a blow with the open hand, an insult as much as an injury
alternatives: a blow with a rod or club
decisions.reason: The word first meant a blow with a stick, but by this time it was commonly used of a slap with the open hand, usually in the face. A slap was a public insult. The same word is used in Mark 14:65 and in 19:3, and in the Greek version of Isaiah 50:6, where the servant of the Lord gives his cheeks to blows. A blow with a rod cannot be ruled out; a footnote gives it.

decisions.choice: Is this how you answer: a rebuke for a lack of respect
alternatives: a real question about the content of the answer
decisions.reason: The officer treats Jesus's words as insolence toward the high priest. The law commanded respect for a ruler of the people (Exodus 22:28, quoted by Paul in a similar scene, Acts 23:2-5).

decisions.choice: the officers: the temple police
decisions.reason: The same men as in verse 18, who served the chief priests (7:32; 18:3, 12).

decisions.choice: temple police (B); temple guards (R); slapped (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the officers as in verse 18. "Slapped" says what kind of blow it most likely was (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: una bofetada
decisions.reason: A blow with the open hand, an insult as much as an injury (meaning decision m1). The officers are named as in verse 18.

decisions.choice: "Anh" from the guard to Jesus, with no setting span
decisions.reason: The guard is rebuking a prisoner and would not say "Ngài"; he uses the plain "anh". The English "you" carries the setting, but a respectful pronoun here would misrepresent the scene.

decisions.choice: The guard rebukes Jesus in the plain style (해라체) and speaks of the high priest with honour (대제사장께)
decisions.reason: The scene is hostile: the guard strikes Jesus, so he does not speak to him as a superior, while showing respect for his own master.

decisions.choice: 뺨을 치다 for "gave a slap"
decisions.reason: A blow to the cheek with the open hand is the insult the meaning note describes; 뺨을 치다 says exactly that.

decisions.choice: tu
decisions.reason: Everyone who speaks to Jesus uses "tu", his opponents included (style section 4); the guard's rebuke and the blow show his attitude. Readable leaves the pronoun out, as the English Readable does.

source.text: ἀπεκρίθη αὐτῷ Ἰησοῦς· Εἰ κακῶς ἐλάλησα, μαρτύρησον περὶ τοῦ κακοῦ· εἰ δὲ καλῶς, τί με δέρεις;

records.literal_gloss: Answered him Jesus, If wrongly I spoke, testify concerning the wrong; if however rightly, why me do you strike?

en.L: Jesus answered him, "If I spoke wrongly, testify concerning the wrong; but if rightly, why do you strike {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?"
en.B: Jesus answered him, "If I said something wrong, then testify to what was wrong. But if I spoke rightly, why do you strike {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?"
en.R: Jesus answered, "If I said something wrong, then be a witness and show everyone what was wrong. But if what I said was right, why do you hit {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?"

es.L: Le respondió Jesús: «Si hablé mal, da testimonio de lo malo; pero si [hablé] bien, ¿por qué {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} golpeas?».
es.B: Jesús le respondió: «Si he dicho algo malo, da testimonio de lo que estuvo mal. Pero si hablé bien, ¿por qué {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} pegas?».
es.R: Jesús respondió: «Si dije algo malo, sé testigo y muéstrales a todos qué fue lo malo. Pero si lo que dije estaba bien, ¿por qué {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} pegas?».

fr.L: Jésus lui répondit : « Si j’ai mal parlé, rends témoignage de ce qui est mal ; mais si [j’ai] bien [parlé], pourquoi {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} frappes-tu ? »
fr.B: Jésus lui répondit : « Si j’ai dit quelque chose de mal, rends témoignage de ce qui était mal. Mais si j’ai bien parlé, pourquoi {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} frappes-tu ? »
fr.R: Jésus a répondu : « Si j’ai dit quelque chose de mal, sois un témoin et montre à tous ce qui était mal. Mais si ce que j’ai dit était juste, pourquoi est-ce que tu {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} frappes ? »

sw.L: Yesu alimjibu, "Kama nilisema vibaya, shuhudia juu ya kile kilichokuwa kibaya; lakini kama [nilisema] vyema, kwa nini unanipiga?"
sw.B: Yesu akamjibu, "Kama nilisema jambo baya, basi shuhudia ni lipi lililokuwa baya. Lakini kama nilisema vyema, kwa nini unanipiga?"
sw.R: Yesu akajibu, "Kama nilisema jambo baya, basi kuwa shahidi uwaonyeshe wote ubaya wake. Lakini kama nilichosema ni sawa, kwa nini unanipiga?"

vi.L: Đức Giê-xu đáp lại người ấy: "Nếu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã nói sai, hãy làm chứng về điều sai; còn nếu [nói] đúng, sao anh đánh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}?"
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu trả lời người ấy: "Nếu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói điều gì sai, thì hãy làm chứng điều sai đó. Còn nếu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói đúng, tại sao anh đánh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}?"
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu trả lời: "Nếu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói điều gì sai, thì anh hãy làm chứng và chỉ ra cho mọi người thấy điều sai đó. Còn nếu điều {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói là đúng, tại sao anh đánh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}?"

ko.L: 예수께서 그에게 대답하셨다. "내가 잘못 말하였다면 그 잘못에 대하여 증언하여라. 그러나 옳게 [말하였다면], 어찌하여 나를 치느냐?"
ko.B: 예수께서 그에게 대답하셨다. "내가 잘못 말했다면 무엇이 잘못되었는지 증언하여라. 그러나 내가 옳게 말했다면 왜 나를 때리느냐?"
ko.R: 예수께서 대답하셨다. "내가 잘못 말했다면 증인이 되어 무엇이 잘못되었는지 모두에게 밝혀라. 그러나 내 말이 옳다면 왜 나를 때리느냐?"

pt.L: Jesus lhe respondeu: "Se falei mal, testemunhe a respeito do mal; mas, se bem, por que você {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} bate?"
pt.B: Jesus lhe respondeu: "Se eu disse algo errado, então testemunhe sobre o que estava errado. Mas, se falei bem, por que você {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} bate?"
pt.R: Jesus respondeu: "Se eu disse alguma coisa errada, então seja testemunha e mostre a todos o que estava errado. Mas, se o que eu disse estava certo, por que você está {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} batendo?"

am.L: ኢየሱስ እንዲህ ብሎ መለሰለት፦ «ክፉ ተናግሬ እንደ ሆነ ስለ ክፉው መስክር፤ በመልካም [ተናግሬ] ከሆነ ግን ስለ ምን ትመታኛለህ?»
am.B: ኢየሱስም እንዲህ ብሎ መለሰለት፦ «የተሳሳተ ነገር ተናግሬ ከሆነ ስሕተቱ ምን እንደ ሆነ መስክር። ትክክል ተናግሬ ከሆነ ግን ለምን ትመታኛለህ?»
am.R: ኢየሱስም እንዲህ ብሎ መለሰ፦ «የተሳሳተ ነገር ከተናገርኩ ምስክር ሆነህ ስሕተቱ ምን እንደ ሆነ ለሁሉም አሳይ። የተናገርኩት ትክክል ከሆነ ግን ለምን ትመታኛለህ?»

hi.L: यीशु ने उसे उत्तर दिया, "यदि मैंने बुरा कहा, तो उस बुराई के विषय में गवाही दो; पर यदि भला [कहा], तो मुझे क्यों मारते हो?"
hi.B: यीशु ने उसे उत्तर दिया, "यदि मैंने कुछ ग़लत कहा, तो गवाही दो कि क्या ग़लत था। पर यदि मैंने ठीक कहा, तो तुम मुझे क्यों मारते हो?"
hi.R: यीशु ने जवाब दिया, "अगर मैंने कुछ ग़लत कहा, तो गवाह बनकर सबको दिखाओ कि क्या ग़लत था। पर अगर मेरी बात ठीक थी, तो तुम मुझे क्यों मार रहे हो?"

ru.L: Иисус ответил ему: «Если {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} сказал худо, засвидетельствуй о худом; если же хорошо, что {{deity_pronoun:меня|Меня}} бьёшь?»
ru.B: Иисус ответил ему: «Если {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} сказал что-то не так, докажи, что было не так. А если {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} сказал верно, за что ты {{deity_pronoun:меня|Меня}} бьёшь?»
ru.R: Иисус ответил: «Если {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} сказал что-то плохое, будь свидетелем и покажи всем, что было плохо. А если {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} сказал правильно, за что ты {{deity_pronoun:меня|Меня}} бьёшь?»

uk.L: Відповів йому Ісус: «Якщо {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} погано сказав, засвідч про погане; а якщо добре, за що {{deity_pronoun:мене|Мене}} бʼєш?»
uk.B: Ісус відповів йому: «Якщо {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} сказав щось не так, засвідч, що саме було не так. А якщо {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} говорив правильно, то за що ти {{deity_pronoun:мене|Мене}} бʼєш?»
uk.R: Ісус відповів: «Якщо {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} сказав щось погане, то будь свідком і покажи всім, що саме було погане. А якщо {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} сказав правильно, то чому ти {{deity_pronoun:мене|Мене}} бʼєш?»

ja.L: イエスは彼に答えられた。「もしわたしが悪く語ったのなら、その悪について証言しなさい。しかし、もし正しく[語った]のなら、なぜわたしを打つのか？」
ja.B: イエスは彼に答えられた。「わたしの言ったことが間違っているなら、何が間違っているのか証言しなさい。正しいことを言ったのなら、なぜわたしを打つのか？」
ja.R: イエスは答えられました。「わたしが何か悪いことを言ったのなら、証人になって、何が悪いのかをみんなに示しなさい。でも、わたしの言ったことが正しいのなら、なぜわたしをたたくのか？」

id.L: Yesus menjawabnya, "Jika {{deity_pronoun:aku|Aku}} salah berkata, buktikanlah kesalahan itu; tetapi jika {{deity_pronoun:aku|Aku}} berkata benar, mengapa engkau memukul {{deity_pronoun:aku|Aku}}?"
id.B: Yesus menjawabnya, "Kalau {{deity_pronoun:aku|Aku}} salah berkata, buktikanlah apa yang salah. Tetapi kalau {{deity_pronoun:aku|Aku}} berkata benar, mengapa engkau memukul {{deity_pronoun:aku|Aku}}?"
id.R: Yesus menjawab, "Kalau {{deity_pronoun:aku|Aku}} mengatakan sesuatu yang salah, jadilah saksi dan tunjukkan kepada semua orang apa yang salah. Tetapi kalau yang {{deity_pronoun:aku|Aku}} katakan benar, mengapa kamu memukul {{deity_pronoun:aku|Aku}}?"

decisions.choice: testify concerning the wrong: give evidence of what was wrong
decisions.reason: The verb is John's word for bearing witness (1:7; 5:31-39; 8:14-18), and here it has its legal sense: if the answer broke the law, let the officer act as a witness and prove it. Jesus asks again for evidence instead of blows (verse 21).

decisions.choice: if wrongly ... if rightly: two possibilities set side by side
decisions.reason: The two conditions do not mean that Jesus is unsure; they put the officer to the test. If he cannot show any wrong, the blow was unjust. "Wrongly" and "rightly" are the common words for badly and well.

decisions.choice: strike: beat or hit
decisions.reason: The verb means to beat or hit someone. Jesus speaks of the blow just given (verse 22); the present tense makes the question vivid: why are you striking me?

decisions.choice: be a witness and show everyone what was wrong
decisions.reason: Readable explains "testify" by what a witness does (meaning decision m1); "everyone" makes plain that testimony is given before others.

decisions.choice: da testimonio (L, B); sé testigo y muéstrales a todos (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep "testimonio", John's witness word throughout, in its legal sense (meaning decision m1). As in English, Readable explains it by what a witness does.

source.text: ἀπέστειλεν οὖν αὐτὸν ὁ Ἅννας δεδεμένον πρὸς Καϊάφαν τὸν ἀρχιερέα.

records.literal_gloss: Sent therefore him Annas bound to Caiaphas the high priest.

en.L: So Annas sent {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} bound to Caiaphas the high priest.
en.B: Then Annas sent {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} on to Caiaphas the high priest, still bound.
en.R: Then Annas sent Jesus to Caiaphas the high priest. Jesus was still tied up.

es.L: Lo envió, pues, Anás atado a Caifás, el sumo sacerdote.
es.B: Entonces Anás {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} envió, todavía atado, a Caifás, el sumo sacerdote.
es.R: Entonces Anás envió a Jesús a Caifás, el sumo sacerdote. Jesús seguía atado.

fr.L: Anne {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}envoya donc, lié, à Caïphe le grand prêtre.
fr.B: Alors Anne {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}envoya, toujours ligoté, à Caïphe, le grand prêtre.
fr.R: Ensuite, Anne a envoyé Jésus à Caïphe, le grand prêtre. Jésus était toujours ligoté.

sw.L: Basi Anasi alimtuma akiwa amefungwa kwa Kayafa kuhani mkuu.
sw.B: Kisha Anasi akamtuma kwa Kayafa kuhani mkuu, akiwa bado amefungwa.
sw.R: Kisha Anasi alimtuma Yesu kwa Kayafa kuhani mkuu. Yesu alikuwa bado amefungwa kamba.

vi.L: Vậy An-ne sai giải {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, bị trói, đến Cai-phe là thầy tế lễ thượng phẩm.
vi.B: Rồi An-ne cho giải {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đến Cai-phe, thầy tế lễ thượng phẩm, mà {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} vẫn còn bị trói.
vi.R: Rồi An-ne giải Đức Giê-xu đến Cai-phe, thầy tế lễ thượng phẩm. Đức Giê-xu vẫn còn bị trói.

ko.L: 그래서 안나스는 그분을 결박한 채로 대제사장 가야바에게 보냈다.
ko.B: 그러자 안나스는 예수를 묶은 그대로 대제사장 가야바에게 보냈다.
ko.R: 그러자 안나스는 예수님을 대제사장 가야바에게 보냈다. 예수님은 여전히 묶여 계셨다.

pt.L: Anás, então, {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} enviou amarrado a Caifás, o sumo sacerdote.
pt.B: Então Anás {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} mandou, ainda amarrado, a Caifás, o sumo sacerdote.
pt.R: Depois Anás mandou Jesus a Caifás, o sumo sacerdote. Jesus ainda estava amarrado.

am.L: ስለዚህ ሐና እንደ ታሠረ ወደ ሊቀ ካህናቱ ወደ ቀያፋ ላከው።
am.B: ከዚያም ሐና ኢየሱስን እንደ ታሠረ ወደ ሊቀ ካህናቱ ወደ ቀያፋ ላከው።
am.R: ከዚያም ሐና ኢየሱስን ወደ ሊቀ ካህናቱ ወደ ቀያፋ ላከው። ኢየሱስ አሁንም እንደ ታሠረ ነበር።

hi.L: तब हन्ना ने उन्हें बँधे हुए ही कैफ़ा महायाजक के पास भेज दिया।
hi.B: तब हन्ना ने उन्हें, बँधे हुए ही, महायाजक कैफ़ा के पास भेज दिया।
hi.R: फिर हन्ना ने यीशु को महायाजक कैफ़ा के पास भेज दिया। यीशु अब भी बँधे हुए थे।

decisions.choice: So Annas sent him: the next step in the story, after the questioning
alternatives: Annas had sent him, so that verses 19-23 took place before Caiaphas
decisions.reason: "So" moves the story on: when the questioning got nowhere, Annas sent Jesus to Caiaphas. Some have read the verb as "had sent", so that the questioning in verses 19-23 took place before Caiaphas; but the Greek tense is the ordinary past for the next event, and the word "so" fits a step forward. Some manuscripts read "and" or have no connecting word, and one early Syriac translation rearranges these verses; the SBLGNT reading is followed. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Annas and Caiaphas: the former high priest and the high priest in office
decisions.reason: Annas was Caiaphas's father-in-law (18:13). Caiaphas was the high priest in office that year (11:49; 18:13), and it was he who had advised that one man should die for the people (18:14). John does not tell what happened before Caiaphas; the next scene is in the morning at Pilate's headquarters (18:28).

decisions.choice: bound: still tied as he had been since the arrest
decisions.reason: Jesus was tied up when he was arrested (18:12). The perfect tense shows that he stayed bound; Annas, though he found no charge, did not set him free.

decisions.choice: still bound (B); Jesus ... still tied up (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "still" to show that he had been bound since the arrest (meaning decision m3). Readable names Jesus and puts his being tied up in a sentence of its own.

decisions.choice: todavía atado (B); Jesús seguía atado (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Balanced and Readable show that he had been bound since the arrest (meaning decision m3). Readable names Jesus.

decisions.choice: they said: the men standing at the fire
decisions.reason: The verb is plural and has no stated subject, so it means the slaves and officers standing with Peter by the fire (verse 18). The other Gospels tell this second question differently (Matthew 26:71; Mark 14:69; Luke 22:58); John says only that several of those present asked it.

decisions.choice: a question that expects the answer no
decisions.reason: The question has the same form as the doorkeeper's (verse 17): "You are not ..., are you?" Again it leaves Peter an easy way to deny.

decisions.choice: the men there
decisions.reason: Readable says who "they" were (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: the question form of verse 17; los hombres que estaban allí (R)
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer no, as in verse 17 (meaning decision m2). Readable says who "they" were (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: "उसके चेलों" (plain)
decisions.reason: The men at the fire speak of Jesus, so they use plain forms, as opponents and bystanders do (style guide, section 7b); the narrator keeps the honorific.

decisions.choice: the men at the fire speak roughly: "おまえ", "あの男", "……ではないだろうな"; also 18:26
decisions.reason: The slaves and officers who arrested Jesus question Peter with suspicion; the rough address marks the rising pressure after the doorkeeper's milder question. The question still expects no (m2).

decisions.choice: denied: disowned Jesus by saying he did not belong to him
decisions.reason: This is the verb Jesus used when he foretold that Peter would deny him three times (13:38). Peter denies not a belief but his own tie to Jesus: "I am not" one of his disciples. John the Baptist is said to have "confessed and not denied" (1:20); Peter does the reverse.

decisions.choice: I am not: the second time Peter says it
decisions.reason: Peter repeats his words of verse 17 (see meaning decision m1 there on the contrast with Jesus's "I am").

decisions.choice: denied [it] (L); denied it (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek verb has no object; English needs "it", which Literal brackets. "Deny" is kept at every level, as in 13:38 at Literal and Balanced, so that the reader sees Jesus's words coming true.

decisions.choice: [lo] negó (L); lo negó (B, R); No soy (L), No lo soy (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek verb has no object; Spanish needs "lo", which Literal brackets. Every level keeps "negar", the verb of 13:38, so that the reader sees Jesus's words coming true (meaning decision m1). Peter's answer as in verse 17.

decisions.choice: kukana at every level, without an object
decisions.reason: "Kukana" is the verb of Jesus's warning in 13:38 ("umenikana mara tatu"), so every level shows his words coming true. Swahili does not need the object that the English Literal brackets. The same in verse 27.

decisions.choice: "отрёкся" at every level
decisions.reason: The verb of 13:38 and of the Synoptic accounts (Matthew 26:70) is kept at every level, so that the reader sees Jesus's word fulfilled; Russian "отречься" needs no object.

decisions.choice: "відректися" (L, B); "заперечити" (R), also in verse 27
decisions.reason: The passion term settled in Matthew: "відректися" keeps the Gospel tradition of Peter's denial; Readable says plainly that he denied it.

decisions.choice: "否定する" (L, B); "打ち消す" (R); also 18:27
decisions.reason: Peter disowns his tie to Jesus (m1). 否定する is the plain word for a denial; Readable uses the everyday 打ち消す.

vi.R: Một người đầy tớ của thầy tế lễ thượng phẩm là bà con của Man-chu, người bị Phi-e-rơ chém đứt tai. Người ấy nói với Phi-e-rơ: "Tôi đã thấy anh ở trong vườn với ông ta, đúng không?"

ko.L: 대제사장의 종들 가운데 하나로서 베드로가 귀를 잘라 버린 [사람]의 친척인 자가 말한다. "내가 동산에서 너를 그와 함께 보지 않았느냐?"
ko.B: 대제사장의 종 가운데 하나로, 베드로가 귀를 잘라 버린 사람의 친척이 말했다. "내가 동산에서 그 사람과 함께 있는 너를 보지 않았느냐?"
ko.R: 대제사장의 종 가운데 한 사람은 말고의 친척이었다. 말고는 베드로가 귀를 잘라 버린 사람이었다. 그가 베드로에게 말했다. "내가 동산에서 그 사람과 함께 있는 너를 분명히 보았다. 그렇지 않으냐?"

pt.L: Diz um dos escravos do sumo sacerdote, sendo parente daquele cuja orelha Pedro cortou: "Eu não vi você no jardim com {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}?"
pt.B: Um dos servos do sumo sacerdote, parente do homem de quem Pedro tinha cortado a orelha, disse: "Eu não vi você com {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} no jardim?"
pt.R: Um dos servos do sumo sacerdote era parente de Malco, o homem que tinha tido a orelha cortada por Pedro. Ele disse a Pedro: "Eu vi você no jardim com {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}, não vi?"

hi.L: महायाजक के दासों में से एक, जो उसका रिश्तेदार था जिसका कान पतरस ने काट डाला था, कहता है, "क्या मैंने तुम्हें उसके साथ बग़ीचे में नहीं देखा?"

hi.R: महायाजक का एक दास मलखुस का रिश्तेदार था, उसी आदमी का जिसका कान पतरस ने काट डाला था। उसने पतरस से कहा, "मैंने तुम्हें बग़ीचे में उसके साथ देखा था, है न?"

ru.L: Говорит один из рабов первосвященника, родственник того, кому Пётр отсёк ухо: «Не я ли видел тебя в саду с {{deity_pronoun:ним|Ним}}?»
ru.B: Один из рабов первосвященника, родственник того человека, которому Пётр отрубил ухо, сказал: «Разве я не видел тебя с {{deity_pronoun:ним|Ним}} в саду?»
ru.R: Один из рабов первосвященника был родственником Малха, того человека, которому Пётр отрубил ухо. Он сказал Петру: «Я же видел тебя в саду с {{deity_pronoun:ним|Ним}}, правда?»

uk.B: Один із рабів первосвященика, родич того, кому Петро відтяв вухо, сказав: «Хіба я не бачив тебе з {{deity_pronoun:ним|Ним}} у саду?»
uk.R: Один із слуг первосвященика був родичем Малха, якому Петро відтяв вухо. Він сказав Петрові: «Я ж бачив тебе в саду з {{deity_pronoun:ним|Ним}}, хіба ні?»

ja.L: 大祭司の奴隷の一人で、ペトロに耳を切り落とされた者の親類である者が言う。「わたしは、園でおまえが彼といっしょにいるのを見なかったか？」
ja.B: 大祭司のしもべの一人で、ペトロに耳を切り落とされた人の親類が言った。「園であの男といっしょにいるのを、わたしは見たではないか？」
ja.R: 大祭司のしもべの一人は、ペトロに耳を切り落とされたマルコスの親類でした。その人がペトロに言いました。「わたしは、おまえが園であの男といっしょにいるのを見た。そうだろう？」

id.L: Salah seorang budak imam besar, seorang kerabat dari orang yang telinganya dipotong Petrus, berkata, "Bukankah aku melihat engkau bersama-sama dengan {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} di taman itu?"
id.B: Salah seorang hamba imam besar, kerabat orang yang telinganya dipotong Petrus, berkata, "Bukankah aku melihat engkau bersama {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} di taman itu?"
id.R: Salah seorang hamba imam besar adalah kerabat Malkhus, orang yang telinganya dipotong Petrus. Dia berkata kepada Petrus, "Aku melihat kamu bersama {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} di taman itu, bukan?"

decisions.choice: a relative of the man whose ear Peter cut off: a kinsman of Malchus
decisions.reason: Peter had cut off the right ear of the high priest's slave Malchus when Jesus was arrested (18:10). This man, a slave of the same household, was a relative of Malchus and had evidently been there in the garden. Of the three who question Peter, he has the most reason to recognize him, and the most reason to be hostile.

decisions.choice: Did I not see you: a question that expects the answer yes, with stress on "I"
alternatives: a question that expects no, like those in verses 17 and 25
decisions.reason: Unlike the first two questions, this one is framed to expect agreement, and the man says "I" with emphasis: I saw you myself. The first two questions gave Peter a way out; this one is a challenge from an eyewitness.

decisions.choice: the garden: the place across the Kidron valley where Jesus was arrested
decisions.reason: John has told that Jesus went with his disciples across the Kidron to a garden, a place where he often met with them (18:1-2), and that he was arrested there.

decisions.choice: Malchus
alternatives: the man whose ear Peter had cut off
decisions.reason: Readable gives the name of the slave, which John has already told the reader (18:10), so that the link is easy to follow; it also puts the question in a form that clearly expects yes (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave".

decisions.choice: ¿No te vi yo ...? (L, B); Yo te vi ..., ¿no es cierto? (R); Malco (R)
decisions.reason: This question expects the answer yes, with stress on "I" (meaning decision m2), which "¿No te vi yo ...?" gives in Spanish. As in English, Readable names Malchus (18:10). "Huerto" as in 18:1.

decisions.choice: a question expecting yes, with stress on "I": "わたしは……見なかったか" (L); "わたしは見たではないか" (B); "わたしは……見た。そうだろう" (R)
alternatives: "見なかったか" at every level
decisions.reason: This question, unlike the first two, expects agreement and stresses "I" (m2). Balanced and Readable say it as an assertion with a tag, which carries that expectation more clearly in Japanese than a negative question.

decisions.choice: the third denial and the rooster: what Jesus foretold has come true
decisions.reason: Jesus had said that a rooster would not crow until Peter had denied him three times (13:38). Now the third denial is made and the rooster crows at once. John does not say what Peter did next; the other Gospels say that he remembered Jesus's words and wept (Matthew 26:75; Mark 14:72; Luke 22:61-62). In John, Peter's story is taken up again after the resurrection (20:2-10; 21:15-19).

decisions.choice: a rooster crowed: the crowing of a bird, in the hours before dawn
alternatives: the Roman trumpet signal at the end of the third watch of the night, called cockcrow
decisions.reason: Roosters crow in the small hours before dawn, and that part of the night could be called "cockcrow" (Mark 13:35). Some have suggested that the trumpet call that marked that watch is meant, but the plain sense is the bird, as Jesus's words in 13:38 suggest. The next scene begins "early" (18:28).

decisions.choice: at that moment (B); Right then (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say that the rooster crowed just as Peter finished speaking, which is what "immediately" means here.

decisions.choice: en ese mismo momento (B); Justo entonces (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: the rooster crowed just as Peter finished speaking. "Cantó un gallo" uses the verb of 13:38 (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: "तुरंत" (L); "उसी समय" (B); "ठीक उसी समय" (R)
decisions.reason: As the style guide settles for the word "immediately" (Mark, section 7b): Literal says "तुरंत", Balanced and Readable say it as the sentence wants. The rooster's crowing is worded as in Mark 14:72 in Hindi.

decisions.choice: "в тот же миг" (B); "тут же" (R)
decisions.reason: As Matthew 26:74 has it: Literal "тотчас пропел петух", Balanced "в тот же миг закричал петух", Readable "тут же запел петух".
